attack_surface.new_input_description: catalog.yaml at a skills-source repo root (author-controlled repo content) supplying a skills_root value that reaches filesystem path joins, git argv pathspecs, tar prefix math, and display strings

findings.title: GET /api/skills/library/status returns raw skills-source URLs to any authenticated principal, including agent-scoped MCP keys; the legacy-adoption path can launder an embedded PAT into that field
findings.description: The status route is gated only by Depends(get_current_user) - no require_admin, no reject_agent_principal, no response_model - while its own siblings on the same router are hardened (/skills/library/{name} calls reject_agent_principal; /skills/sources is require_admin). Its body carries per-source raw url plus the legacy flat url with no userinfo stripping on any reader. Separately, _adopt_legacy_clone migrates the pre-ent#237 skills_library_url setting into a skill_sources row without reject_embedded_credentials or validate_skills_library_url, both of which the POST/PUT source routes do apply. The legacy setter (PUT /api/settings/{key}) validated only via validate_skills_library_url, which checks parsed.hostname and therefore ignores userinfo - empirically confirmed to return a PAT-bearing URL unchanged. url_validation.py:31 documents that embedded-credential rejection was deliberately kept out of that helper so upgrading installs relying on an embedded token would not break, i.e. the codebase asserts such installs plausibly exist.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) An operator configured skills_library_url as https://<pat>@github.com/org/private-skills before ent#237 - accepted without complaint. 2) Any sync runs (admin-triggered or the ent#236 auto-sync); adoption writes the PAT-bearing URL verbatim into skill_sources and deletes the legacy setting, making the row the durable home. 3) An attacker holding ANY authenticated principal - a user-role chat-only grantee created via /share, or any non-ephemeral agent-scoped MCP key reached by prompt injection inside any agent workspace (the MCP tool get_skills_library_status has no canAccess gate and is advertised to every agent key) - calls GET /api/skills/library/status and reads sources[].url in cleartext. No further action needed.
findings.impact: Discloses a GitHub PAT with at least private-repo read to the lowest-privilege role and to untrusted agent workspaces. Unconditional lesser variant: private skills-repo URLs (org/repo names) are disclosed to every authenticated principal even with no PAT present.
findings.recommendation: (a) Add require_admin + reject_agent_principal to /skills/library/status, or strip userinfo from url in get_library_status before returning (skill_service.py:891,942). (b) Call reject_embedded_credentials in _adopt_legacy_clone and either refuse adoption or strip userinfo before create_skill_source (skill_service.py:560). Fix belongs on the ent#237 branch (still unmerged - the cheap moment), not this PR.
findings.verification: Independent fresh-context refutation agent attempted six distinct refutations; all failed. Route gate, absence of redaction, adoption bypass, reachability of the misconfiguration precondition, absence of any userinfo stripper, and agent-key reachability each confirmed with file:line citations.

clean_categories.P2_secrets: No secret-shaped tokens introduced by the diff (word-boundary scan for sk-/ghp_/gho_/github_pat_/xox[bp]-/AKIA/PRIVATE KEY on added lines: zero hits). No .env or CI config touched.
clean_categories.P9_A01_access_control: Zero endpoints, auth dependencies, or route decorators added or altered by the diff (routers/skills.py untouched).
clean_categories.P9_A03_injection: The author-controlled skills_root reaches git argv only as a pathspec behind an explicit -- separator at both call sites (skill_source_clone.py:556,581; clone at :254 already had it), never through a shell - subprocess list form throughout. Segment-wise validation rejects a leading '-' so the value can never read as an option.
clean_categories.P9_A03_path_traversal: Actively verified: no member name under any source_root can escape the destination prefix. Attack corpus (skills/x/../../../../etc/passwd, skills/x/../../.env, skills/x/a/../../../outside) produced zero escapes; every unsafe source_root (../../etc, skills/../.., '.', -oProxyCommand=x, /etc, a//b) raises ValueError rather than silently mis-prefixing.
clean_categories.P9_A08_integrity: catalog.yaml parses through the shared ent#314 hardened loader with AliasPolicy.REJECT and a 64 KB cap, enforced by a bounded read(cap+1) - a post-read length check would be defeated by a symlinked catalog.yaml. The ent#314 consolidation guard remains green (21 passed); no new bare yaml.safe_load on author-controlled content.
clean_categories.P7_llm_agent_isolation: The author-controlled root never reaches an in-container exec. All five in-agent scripts hardcode ~/.claude/skills (skill_service.py:1042,1076,1191,1212,1276); the arcname rewrite at filter_skill_archive means the restore paths allowlist, manifest, prune confinement and gitignore lines stay destination-canonical regardless of source layout.
clean_categories.P7_protected_names: Protected-basename enforcement survives the rewrite (checked on the pre-rewrite relative path): .env, CLAUDE.md and .trinity-skill.json under a custom root are still dropped with named warnings.
clean_categories.P9_A03_xss: No v-html on the skills surfaces; the new skills_root/layout_conflict fields and the now-variable path string are plain interpolation (Vue auto-escaped) and charset-restricted to [A-Za-z0-9._-] per segment.
clean_categories.P5_vendored_parity: Invariant #5 unaffected - zero docker/base-image files touched, no vendored security-policy copy modified.
clean_categories.P9_A09_logging: Author-controlled values reaching logs use %r (repr-escaped, defeating newline log-injection) and are bounded by the 64 KB catalog cap. No credential material logged.

below_gate_notes: skills_root echoed into logs via %r without truncation - bounded by the 64 KB catalog cap and repr-escaped; hardening nicety, confidence 3/10, not a finding.
